topic.subject: social
topic.title: Development
topic.scope: different goals, national and per capita income, HDI, literacy and infant mortality, sustainability

misconceptions.statement: A higher per capita income means everyone in the country is equally rich.
misconceptions.why: Students confuse the mathematical average with an equal distribution of wealth.
misconceptions.fix: Per capita income is an average; it does not show how income is distributed among the rich and the poor.

probe.question: If Country A has a higher average income than Country B, is every citizen in A richer than in B?
probe.wrong_answer: Yes, because the average is higher.

misconceptions.root_belief: Averages represent the status of every individual.

misconceptions.statement: Development is only about earning more money.
misconceptions.why: Students equate economic growth with the broader concept of human development.
misconceptions.fix: Development includes non-material goals like freedom, security, equal treatment, and a clean environment.

probe.question: Which is a better measure of development: salary or freedom and health?

misconceptions.root_belief: Money is the sole indicator of success.

misconceptions.statement: Sustainability means we should stop using all natural resources.
misconceptions.why: Students interpret 'sustainability' as 'total preservation' rather than 'judicious use'.
misconceptions.fix: Sustainability means using resources in a way that meets current needs without compromising the ability of future generations to meet theirs.

probe.question: Is sustainable development about stopping all mining?
probe.wrong_answer: Yes, we must stop using resources to save them.

misconceptions.statement: Literacy rate is the percentage of people who can write their name.
misconceptions.why: Students confuse basic literacy with functional literacy.
misconceptions.fix: Literacy rate measures the proportion of the 7-year-old and above population that can read and write with understanding in any language.

probe.question: Who is counted as literate?
probe.wrong_answer: Anyone who can sign their name.

misconceptions.root_belief: A word means its everyday meaning.

misconceptions.statement: Per capita income is the total income earned by the whole country.
misconceptions.why: Students confuse 'per capita' with the national total and ignore that it is divided by population.
misconceptions.fix: Per capita income is the country's total income divided by its total population, so it is the average income per person.

probe.question: A country earns a total of Rs 10,00,000 crore and has 100 crore people. What is its per capita income?
probe.wrong_answer: Rs 10,00,000 crore, because per capita income is the total income of the country.

misconceptions.root_belief: per capita means total, not average per person

misconceptions.statement: A country with a larger population always has a higher per capita income.
misconceptions.why: Students link a big population with a big economy and forget that population is the divisor.
misconceptions.fix: For the same total income, a larger population gives a lower per capita income because the income is shared among more people.

probe.question: Two countries have the same total income, but country A has twice the population of country B. Which has the higher per capita income?
probe.wrong_answer: Country A, because more people means more income per person.

misconceptions.root_belief: more people always means more income per person

misconceptions.statement: HDI is calculated only from a country's income and wealth.
misconceptions.why: Students carry over the idea of income as the only measure of development and ignore the other HDI components.
misconceptions.fix: HDI combines three parts: health (life expectancy), education (years of schooling) and standard of living (per capita income).

probe.question: Name the components used to calculate the Human Development Index.
probe.wrong_answer: Only GDP and per capita income, since HDI measures how rich a country is.

misconceptions.root_belief: HDI is just another income measure

misconceptions.statement: The HDI rank is given by the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP), and the World Bank prepares it.
misconceptions.why: Students mix up the UNDP, which publishes the Human Development Report, with the World Bank, which classifies countries by income.
misconceptions.fix: The UNDP publishes the Human Development Report and HDI rankings. The World Bank classifies countries by income as rich or low-income.

probe.question: Which organisation publishes the Human Development Report with HDI rankings?
probe.wrong_answer: The World Bank publishes the Human Development Report.

misconceptions.root_belief: all international development bodies do the same work

misconceptions.statement: Groundwater and fossil fuels are renewable resources that will never run out.
misconceptions.why: Students see water and fuel as always available and mix up renewable and non-renewable resources.
misconceptions.fix: Groundwater is used faster than it is replenished in many places, and fossil fuels take millions of years to form, so overuse depletes them.

probe.question: Why do experts warn about falling groundwater levels in Punjab and Haryana?
probe.wrong_answer: They need not worry, because groundwater is renewable and always refills itself however much is used.

misconceptions.root_belief: renewable means unlimited whatever the rate of use

misconceptions.statement: A country with a high per capita income must also have good health and education.
misconceptions.why: Students assume income automatically buys good health and schooling for everyone.
misconceptions.fix: Income does not buy everything. Kerala has a lower per capita income than Haryana but a better literacy rate and a lower infant mortality rate. Public facilities like schools and health centres matter.

probe.question: Haryana has a higher per capita income than Kerala. Which state has the better literacy rate and lower IMR?
probe.wrong_answer: Haryana, since its higher income gives better schools and hospitals.

misconceptions.root_belief: money alone guarantees health and education

misconceptions.statement: If the average income of a country is high, then every person in it earns near that average.
misconceptions.why: Students read an average as a typical value and miss that a few very rich people can pull it up.
misconceptions.fix: An average hides differences. Some people may earn far more and others far less than the average, so look at the distribution too.

probe.question: Five people earn Rs 1,000 each and one earns Rs 25,000. The average is Rs 5,000. Is it a good picture of what most of them earn?
probe.wrong_answer: Yes, most people in the group earn about Rs 5,000.

misconceptions.root_belief: an average represents each individual's value

misconceptions.statement: Infant Mortality Rate is the number of infants who die out of every 100 people in the country.
misconceptions.why: Students mix up the base for IMR with percentages of the whole population.
misconceptions.fix: IMR is the number of children who die before the age of one year, per 1000 live births in that year.

probe.question: What does an IMR of 30 mean?
probe.wrong_answer: Thirty out of every hundred people in the country die in infancy.

misconceptions.root_belief: rates are always per hundred of the whole population
